aep_note: AEP DOES have usable international service to Lima - this is the single most useful finding in this research, and it contradicts the common assumption (and the currently-stale English Wikipedia destinations table for Aeroparque). Since Argentina opened Aeroparque to regional international traffic (Mercosur plus Peru and Colombia), AEP-LIM has become a heavily served nonstop market: roughly 18 weekly departures AEP-LIM and 22 weekly LIM-AEP, flown by FOUR carriers - Aerolineas Argentinas (AR1364/AR1365), LATAM (LA2464/LA2381/LA2368 out, LA2465/LA2445/LA2380/LA2369 back), JetSMART (JA7801/JA7800) and Sky Airline (H2 5810/H2 5811). Aerolineas Argentinas in fact serves Lima ONLY from Aeroparque - it has no EZE-LIM nonstop. Ezeiza has its own separate nonstops (LATAM LA2376 and LA2946, Sky H2 5800, and JetSMART daily from 01 Jan 2027). Practical read for a group of 5 living in Buenos Aires: AEP is ~10 min and a few thousand pesos from Palermo/Belgrano versus ~50-70 min and ~USD 30-40 by remis to Ezeiza, so a marginally higher AEP fare is often the cheaper door-to-door trip. Verify the airport on every quote before booking - some OTAs show 'BUE' and you will only discover which terminal at checkout.
seasonality_note: Two different seasonal clocks are at work. (1) AIRFARE from Buenos Aires is driven by ARGENTINE outbound demand: January and December are peak (Kayak logs ~USD 520-529 RT average for January, ~USD 460 for December), the market breaks sharply once Argentine schools go back at the start of March, and June is the annual floor (~USD 352-360). Sky Airline's own booking engine makes the cliff explicit: a BUE-LIM lead-in of USD 396 RT for February 2027 versus USD 220 RT for March 2027. That is why W2 and W3 are materially cheaper than W1, and why moving the W1 departure from Fri 26 Feb to the following weekend is worth roughly USD 60-70 per person, i.e. USD 300-350 for the group. (2) WEATHER: late Feb/March is the tail of the Peruvian coastal summer. Mancora and the whole north coast are at their best - March is statistically the hottest month there (avg ~27C, highs to 31C) with the warmest sea of the year (~25C in mid-March), which makes W3 the best window for the beach even though it is not the cheapest. The only caveat is that March is also the wettest month on the north coast (~35 mm over ~5 days) and an El Nino year would make that much worse. Lima at the same time is at the end of its summer: warm (25-28C), humid, hazy, and the garua fog season begins in April, so late Feb/March is genuinely the last good stretch for Lima's beaches and rooftops. For the Andes (Cusco, Machu Picchu) this is the WET season and low season - relevant only if anyone wants to bolt on a Cusco leg. Finally, book by late October 2026: both Kayak and the airlines' own data put the optimal booking point at 18-24 weeks out, worth roughly 23-25% versus a late booking, and a 5-seat block is exactly what disappears first in a cheap fare bucket. One date trap: Easter Sunday 2027 is 28 March, so Semana Santa runs 21-28 March. W3's optional Sun 21 Mar return is Palm Sunday and will price and fill accordingly - return Sat 20 Mar instead.

verdict.recommendation: W2 (Sat 6 Mar - Sat 13 Mar 2027), nonstop, JetSMART or Sky ex-AEP, ~USD 270-295 pp RT. Add a LIM-TBP or LIM-TYL round trip at ~USD 130-150 pp for Mancora. Total air budget ~USD 400-445 pp, ~USD 2,000-2,225 for the group of 5.
verdict.internal_verdict: Fly LIM-TBP (Tumbes) or LIM-TYL (Talara) for Mancora - both are 1h50-1h55 nonstop on LATAM or Sky, 4-6 daily, USD 130-150 RT. Talara is 30 min closer to Mancora; Tumbes has more frequency and is usually slightly cheaper. Paracas is NOT flyable: Pisco has no scheduled commercial service, so it is a 3h15m road transfer from Lima.
verdict.one_stop_verdict: One-stops via Santiago exist and are real, but the saving is only USD 25-35 per person for 4-6 extra hours each way. With JetSMART and Sky now flying EZE-LIM and AEP-LIM nonstop at LCC prices, the classic 'connect to save' play is dead on this route. Book nonstop.
